chunks: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Maqri, from Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Maqani, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abd al-Mu'min, from al-Harith ibn Hasira, from Ammarah ibn Juwayn al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say from the pulpit: The Mahdi is from my progeny, from my Ahl al-Bayt. He will emerge in the last period of time. Rain will descend for him from the sky, and the earth will bring forth its vegetation for him. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as the people had filled it with injustice and oppression.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family and Imams
key_terms.الظُّلْم: Injustice or oppression, the state of the world before the Mahdi
key_terms.الْجَوْر: Deviation from truth or tyranny, often paired with oppression
key_terms.الْقِسْط: Equity or fair distribution, often paired with justice (adl)
key_terms.الْمَهْدِي: The Guided One, a specific title for the twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.عِتْرَة: Progeny or descendants, specifically referring to the Prophet's family

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and characteristics of the Mahdi's emergence according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri establishes the Mahdi’s lineage from the Ahl al-Bayt, a core tenet of Shia eschatology. It highlights the dual nature of his emergence: divine natural facilitation through rain and earth's produce, alongside his political mission to restore justice (*adl*) and equity (*qist*) to a world saturated with tyranny. This narration serves as a primary proof for the Mahdi’s role as the ultimate restorer of divine order in the end times.
